client: Codex CLI 0.151.0, installed Debian package and explicit skill
platform: Debian 12 amd64 container joined to a route-free hostile DNS/HTTP fixture namespace
checks: old package launch and loopback denial
harness_issue_and_fix: The initial umask 077 run reached all native calls but failed when the ordinary probe could not hash root-owned 0600 capture bytes. Pre-creating the capture as the probe owner fixed that read, but privileged tshark could not open the private user-owned capture. Reading it with ordinary-user tshark inside the private probe directory fixed the parser; the final identical restrictive-umask replay passed. Each failed run cleaned up its owned container and namespace.
limits: The capture was confined to the fixture namespace and then deleted; the hash is a record, not independently inspectable retained evidence. It excludes host-client and other-tool traffic. Two deterministic answers do not prove all rebinding schedules or resolver behavior. The package upgrade changed package metadata but not executable bytes, so it is not a changed-binary compatibility test. RSS/FD observations are finite samples. This does not qualify an official release candidate, the owner's residual-risk acceptance, or any of the four AI Scraping Defense repositories.
